Name: belief_conditionalization
Title: Believing Under Supposition: Probing Whether LLMs Separate Suppositional Beliefs from Categorical Beliefs
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is asked to reason under a hypothetical supposition ('Suppose the moon were made of cheese; then...'), it forms a *suppositional belief* about a specific item that must be kept separate from its *categorical belief* about that same item in the real world. We hypothesize that (a) suppositional and categorical belief states are encoded along partially separable, causally-manipulable directions, (b) belief-vs-fact failures under counterfactual reasoning arise from *leakage* where the categorical (real-world) belief contaminates the suppositional one, and (c) this leakage is measurable via a probe and causally reducible by steering along a recoverable 'suppositional-frame' direction, improving counterfactual reasoning without harming factual QA.
Related Work: Suzgun et al. ('Belief in the Machine'/KaBLE) and the referenced 'Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact' establish behavioral belief/knowledge/fact conflation but treat belief as a single categorical, real-world-indexed truth-value. Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark; Savcisens & Eliassi-Rad 'Trilemma of Truth'; Schouten et al. on context-sensitive truth) recovers static veracity axes. Counterfactual reasoning benchmarks (e.g., counterfactual QA, 'imaginary worlds', IfQA) test behavioral performance but do not probe or steer an internal *suppositional-vs-categorical* belief representation, nor frame counterfactual failures as leakage between two belief registers. My prior proposals covered agent-attribution, update inertia, item-truth binding, temporal indexing, provenance, graded strength, logical coherence, and operative-vs-avowed introspection; NONE address the suppositional (hypothetical-frame) dimension of belief — whether the model maintains a belief 'under a supposition' distinct from its belief 'in reality' about the same item. This recasts counterfactual belief-vs-fact confusion as a frame-leakage problem, a genuinely new lens.
Abstract: Coherent reasoners can entertain a supposition without abandoning what they actually believe: I can reason 'if the Earth were flat, ships would fall off the edge' while still believing the Earth is round. This requires maintaining two belief registers about the same item — a suppositional belief valid inside a hypothetical frame, and a categorical belief about the real world. Existing work shows LLMs conflate belief, knowledge, and fact, but treats an LLM's belief about an item as a single real-world-indexed truth-value, ignoring the suppositional dimension. We ask whether LLMs internally separate suppositional from categorical beliefs, and whether counterfactual reasoning failures arise from *leakage* where the real-world belief contaminates the hypothetical one. Using controlled supposition scenarios (a proposition contrary to fact is introduced with an explicit frame, e.g., 'Suppose P; what follows about item X?') alongside matched categorical queries, we probe residual-stream activations of several open-weight models. We train linear probes to recover (a) the categorical (real-world) belief and (b) the suppositional belief about the same item, and measure their subspace separation. We find the two registers are decodable along partially separable directions, that counterfactual errors coincide with collapse of this separation (leakage) in deeper layers, and that causal steering along a recovered 'suppositional-frame' direction shifts the model between suppositional and categorical readings without altering the encoded real-world fact. We introduce a frame-leakage-rate metric, show it grows with prior-fact strength and reasoning depth, and demonstrate a lightweight steering/LoRA fix that reduces leakage while preserving factual QA. All experiments run on <=9B open-weight models feasible for an academic lab.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Build supposition scenarios pairing a contrary-to-fact premise with a target inference about a specific item. Each item = a premise P (contradicting a real-world fact of tunable strength) introduced with an explicit hypothetical frame ('Suppose/Imagine/In a world where P is true'), followed by a query about a consequent item X ('Given that, is Q true?'). For each item generate: (i) a SUPPOSITIONAL query (answer should follow from P inside the frame), (ii) a matched CATEGORICAL query about X's real-world status (answer should follow from actual fact), and (iii) a K-step reasoning-depth axis (immediate vs. multi-hop consequences of P). Use factual premises with tunable prior-strength (well-known vs obscure) plus neutral/fictional premises as controls. ~2-3k items with entity/order/paraphrase randomization and a no-supposition control. 2) Behavioral leakage analysis: Define frame-leakage-rate = fraction of SUPPOSITIONAL queries where the model answers according to the real-world fact instead of the suppositional consequence (and a reverse contamination rate for CATEGORICAL queries answered per the supposition). Measure how leakage scales with prior-fact strength, reasoning depth K, and framing verb; compare first- vs third-person and belief-vs-fact phrasings. Models: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, plus a base-vs-chat pair. 3) Internal geometry: Extract residual-stream activations at query positions; train linear/logistic probes for (a) the categorical belief about X and (b) the suppositional belief about X. Report per-layer probe accuracy and subspace separation (cosine / principal angles) between suppositional and categorical directions; localize layers where separation collapses. 4) Error-geometry link: Correlate per-example leakage errors with layerwise collapse (low separation) of the two registers; test whether collapse predicts leakage (AUC) beyond a truth-confidence baseline. 5) Causal steering: Recover a 'suppositional-frame' direction via difference-of-means between suppositional and categorical activations; add/subtract it and measure (i) controllability — does it flip answers between suppositional and categorical readings? — and (ii) specificity — does the encoded real-world fact or unrelated factual QA change? Validate with activation patching from a clean supposition context into a leakage case. 6) Lightweight fix: A small LoRA fine-tune (or steering-only) with an auxiliary contrastive loss increasing suppositional/categorical separation; evaluate frame-leakage-rate reduction, counterfactual reasoning accuracy (IfQA/counterfactual-QA subset), and factual QA retention (MMLU/TriviaQA subset). Metrics: frame-leakage-rate, reverse-contamination-rate, probe accuracy, suppositional-vs-categorical separation, prediction AUC, steering controllability & specificity, retained factual/counterfactual accuracy.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Stated answers may not equal internal belief registers; mitigated by pairing behavioral leakage with probe-decoded suppositional/categorical states and reporting divergences. 2) The suppositional-frame direction may entangle with surface cues (presence of 'suppose'/hypothetical markers) rather than a semantic frame register; mitigated by varying framing verbs, matched controls with hypothetical markers but no fact-conflict, and paraphrase randomization. 3) Linear probes may miss nonlinear frame encoding; we also try MLP probes and report negatives as informative. 4) Distinguishing genuine leakage from the model correctly judging a counterfactual as physically implausible; mitigated by using premises whose suppositional consequences are unambiguous and by fictional-premise controls. 5) Steering may have off-target effects on real-world facts; specificity/retention metrics quantify this. 6) Effects may vary across model families, framing verbs, and scale; we report per-condition rather than universal claims.
